L419 | **Origin.** With \(\operatorname{Attempt}(s,c,p,h,e)\) the relation that \(c\) is actually used to address \(p\),
L420 |
L421 | \[
L422 | \operatorname{Origin}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,p,h,e)\iff\operatorname{Attempt}(s,c,p,h,e)\land\operatorname{New}(s,c,h,e)\land\operatorname{Build}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,h,e). \tag{G}
L423 | \]
L424 |
L425 | The content \(c\) may be an organization, a transport, or a contract. When it is a contract, the originative act is the finding of a question. A dimension of variation mentioned in passing is not thereby a port of the account; it becomes one when the account admits changes to it, and adding it is construction.
L426 |
L427 | **Ownership.** The subhistory in Build is owned by \(s\) when its processes run inside the system boundary and resource contract declared for \(s\) (Part XII). Work supplied from outside that boundary, a diagnosis, a decisive question, an instruction about what to read, remains an outside contribution however it is executed inside; a process that runs inside the boundary is the system's own whoever wrote it; and where the boundary is drawn decides, not where the process sits in the casing. Contribution of content and ownership of a process are different attributions: a routine written outside the boundary and run inside it is the system's own process, and its content remains its writer's contribution. Ownership is not defined by the capability attributed through it (Part XII).
L428 |
L429 | **Episodes.** A complete critical episode contains a recognized difficulty, a target available before its criticism, a conjectural objection, and a content-sensitive response. A **recognized difficulty** is a failure of a claimed aim, or a conflict in which what the system holds meets a claimed aim only by failing a protected one (Part XI), when the system represents it. A creative critical episode contains an instance of (G) connected to its inquiry. Closing an episode is a choice: an argument can rule out some ways of closing it for the person choosing, and where it leaves one way not ruled out, the person sees no option but that one, which is not to say the person has no option; no argument makes the choice.
L430 |
L431 | ---
L432 |
L433 | # Part XI — Repair, created explanation, and appraisal
L434 |
L435 | **Repair.** The contribution \(\Delta\) of a repair is a subhistory together with the changes of content it makes. For claimed aims \(O\) and protected aims \(P\), fixed for the comparison,
L436 |
L437 | \[
L438 | \operatorname{Repair}_{O,P}(\xi,\xi';\Delta)\iff\exists o\in O[\neg o(\xi)\land o(\xi')]\land\forall r\in P[r(\xi)\Rightarrow r(\xi')]\land\operatorname{ProducedBy}(\Delta,\xi,\xi';O). \tag{P}
L439 | \]
L440 |
L441* | The aims are declared inputs: \(O\) says what is to be repaired and \(P\) what is to be protected, each as a stated condition over stated occasions, and \(\operatorname{Lost}_{\xi,\xi'}(r)\iff r(\xi)\land\neg r(\xi')\) (D14.1). In (P), accordingly, \(r(\xi')\) says of a protected condition \(r\) that it was met on every occasion it covers from \(\xi\) to \(\xi'\), not only at \(\xi'\). Their declaration makes no appraisal of the aims, and (P) puts no order on alternatives. Losses outside \(P\) must be exposed. \(\operatorname{ProducedBy}\) is met when an active route (Part IX) runs from \(\Delta\) to the repair; it attributes the repair to each contribution whose active route ran to it in the history, and where two sufficient contributions both ran, the repair is attributed to both and the history supplies no division of the attribution that it does not contain. An account that produced nothing, an act that repaired without an account, and a repair produced through use of an account are three different attributions.
L442 |
L443 | **Created explanation.** An explanatory aim requires a deployable account, or the correction of a use through one. With \(O_{\mathrm{ex}}\subseteq O\) the explanatory aims,
L444 |
L445 | \[
L446 | \begin{aligned}
L447 | \operatorname{CreateEx}(s,\Delta,h,e)\iff{}&\operatorname{CreativeCriticalEpisode}(s,\Delta,h,e)\land\exists\xi,\xi'\,\bigl[\operatorname{Repair}_{O,P}(\xi,\xi';\Delta)\\
L448 | &\land\exists o\in O_{\mathrm{ex}}\,\exists c,p_c,e_c,t_c,\Gamma_c\,[e_c\preceq_h e\land\neg o(\xi)\land o(\xi')\land\operatorname{Origin}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,p_c,h,e_c)\\
L449 | &\quad\land\operatorname{Account}\big((c,p_c,t_c,\Gamma_c)\big)\land c\in\operatorname{Result}(\Delta)\land\operatorname{Deploy}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,\xi';U_c)\land\operatorname{ProducesVia}(\Delta,c,o;\xi,\xi')]\bigr].
L450 | \end{aligned}\tag{EX}
L451 | \]
L452 |
L453* | \(\operatorname{Result}(\Delta)\) is the set of contents at \(\xi'\) that \(\Delta\) prepared. \(\operatorname{ProducesVia}(\Delta,c,o;\xi,\xi')\) is met when an active route that runs from \(\Delta\) to the repair of \(o\) contains the relevant binding of \(c\) (D14.6). In (EX), \(t_c\) and \(\Gamma_c\) are the transport and the identified commitments that make \(c\), with \(p_c\), an explanatory candidate (Part V), and \(U_c\) is the declared use task for \(c\) (Deploy, Part X). The scope of \(\operatorname{Account}((c,p_c,t_c,\Gamma_c))\) is the contract fixed at \(e_c\). A later narrowing of that contract to rescue \(c\)'s meeting (E) is a new claim at a new index, and does not retroactively meet (EX).
L454 |
L455 | **Appraisal.** Repairing an aim repairs it and says nothing about how anyone appraises the aim, or the question that led to it. Where a claim invokes an appraisal, the semantics takes the **appraisal relation** \(\mathcal N\) (import 2, Part XIV) as an input and marks the place. The aesthetic case is one such invocation: an effect organization \(\mathcal R\subseteq \mathit{Act}\times\mathit{Occ}\times\mathit{Eff}\); a purpose \(G\subseteq \mathit{Occ}\times\mathit{Eff}\); achievement \(\mathcal R[a,k]\neq\varnothing\land\mathcal R[a,k]\subseteq G[k]\) (AR); and \(\mathcal N\subseteq \mathit{Act}\times\mathit{Occ}\times\mathsf{Rsn}\times\mathcal V_A\) taken as a substantive input when aesthetic value is claimed, where \(\mathit{Act}\) is a set of actions, \(\mathit{Occ}\) of occasions, \(\mathit{Eff}\) of effects, \(\mathsf{Rsn}\) of aesthetic reasons and \(\mathcal V_A\) of aesthetic values, the last two not further specified here. None is defined as another. The semantics does not define \(\mathcal N\), and no aesthetics follows from achieving a stated effect.
L456 |
L457 | ---
L458 |
L459 | # Part XII — The physical module
L460 |
L461 | **Tasks.** A substrate is a physical system; an attribute a set of its states; a task a specified input-to-output attribute transformation with explicit resources and side effects. Possibility is the absence of a law-imposed limit, short of exact, on the tolerance to which a task can be performed and retained; it is not one trajectory that performed the task. The physical module adopts a task-based formulation of physics for this purpose. It is where physical possibility enters the semantics as instantiation and transformation; it also enters as the content of claims a candidate can conflict with (Part VI). The module says which organizations a carrier can instantiate, and which transformations of a content, such as holding, copying, teaching, testing, building or performing it, can be carried out. It does not define a question, an account or a conflict between candidates (Parts III, V, VI).
L462 |
L463 | **Retained realization.** For protocol \(\pi\), task \(T\), constructor attribute \(C\), and enabling conditions \(\chi\),
L464 |
L465 | \[
L466 | \operatorname{RetReal}(\pi,T,C;\chi)\iff\forall z\in C\ \forall i\in\operatorname{dom}T\ \forall\eta\in\operatorname{Exec}(\pi,z,i;\chi),\ \eta\text{ completes with }o\in T[i]\text{ and }z'\in C. \tag{CT1}
L467 | \]
L468 |
L469 | Execution families are nonempty on admitted inputs; deadlock is not a vacuous performance of the task.
L470 |
L471* | **Retention fixed point.** \(F(C)=\{z:\forall i\in\operatorname{dom}T\ \forall\eta\in\operatorname{Exec}(\pi,z,i;\chi),\ \eta\text{ completes with }o\in T[i]\text{ and }z'\in C\}\). \(F\) is monotone; \(C\subseteq F(C)\) is the invariant form; the greatest fixed point is the union of the sets \(D\) with \(D\subseteq F(D)\). (CT2)
L472 |
L473 | **System boundary and continuity.** A capability is attributed to a system under a declared boundary (which processes and resources are the system's) and a declared continuity \(\Omega\) (what makes it the same system through change). A replaced part that preserves the declared continuity leaves the same system; a process run inside the boundary is the system's whoever wrote it; a process run outside it is not the system's however close it sits. Both are declared before the attribution, not chosen after it. Where the system's boundary is not declared explicitly, a statement that names the system and says whether a process runs inside it or outside it declares the boundary for that process; a statement that the process is the system's own, which does not say where it runs, is the attribution, not its boundary.
L474 |
L475 | **Owned capability.** \(\operatorname{Can}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi,T;\chi)\) requires an owned retained realization or an owned, physically admitted, finite construction of one under the same continuity and resource contract. A theorist's description of a protocol is not the system's possession of it. Ownership is defined by the processes and resources the boundary includes, never by the capability being attributed: "owned because it can, and can because owned" defines neither.
L476 |
L477 | **Achievement.** \(\operatorname{CanAdv}(\xi,p;\chi,J_p,C_I)\): for each starting configuration in the independently specified \(J_p\), every maximal execution completes with a history meeting the achievement predicate and a continuing organization in \(C_I\). A first discovery is not a repeatable task; retention is applied to the inquiry-enabling organization. (CA)
L478 |
L479 | **Tolerances.** The tolerances of the physical module (Part XIV) form a directed preorder \(Q_\Theta\), in which \(q\) precedes \(q'\) when \(q'\) admits no performance \(q\) excludes, and none of them is exact; \(q\in Q_\Theta\) is a tolerance of performance and \(r\in Q_\Theta\) a tolerance of retention. \(\mathsf{Admit}^{q,r}_\Theta\) is the set of tasks physically achievable at tolerances \((q,r)\); \(\mathsf{Cap}^{q,r}_\Omega(\xi)\) is the set of tasks with an owned realization, or an owned construction of one, at those tolerances, as owned capability requires; and \(\mathsf{Poss}_\Theta=\bigcap_{q,r}\mathsf{Admit}^{q,r}_\Theta\) is the set of tasks achievable at every tolerance, which is what possibility means under Tasks. Then \(\mathsf{Cap}^{q,r}_\Omega(\xi)\subseteq\mathsf{Admit}^{q,r}_\Theta\); \(\mathsf{Cap}^\infty=\bigcap_{q,r}\mathsf{Cap}^{q,r}\subseteq\mathsf{Poss}_\Theta\). (CT3, CT4) Capability at a given tolerance does not imply possibility at every tolerance.
L480 |
L481 | **Selection in the physical module.** A selected provenance \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\) is a claim about a physical history: a population of candidate transports, a physically admitted variation operator, and a survival condition enacted by the environment. It is fallible and testable as any physical claim is. The population is the set of transports the physics and the stated construction admit; a transport that would need a part every member of the population is built without is not in it.

L485 | # Part XIII — Recursion and universality

L487 | **Scrutinizability.** An aspect \(d\) of a system's practice is scrutinizable at \(\xi\) when there is an owned, admitted continuation in which a description of \(d\) becomes a represented target, criticism can be directed at it, and the result can affect its operative use. L489 | **Recursive capacity.**
L490 |
L491 | \[

L539 |
L540 | **(Elim) Reinstatement of kinds.** A case where a kind-label distinguishes two accounts that no admitted change distinguishes, and the distinction does explanatory work. L541 |
L542 | **(Prov) Genesis.** Any of three: a selected transport whose value at an unseen change is determined by its history although its population admits a differing survivor there (against Argument 3; a population with no such survivor is the claim's own qualification, not an argument that rules it out); a method that rewrites every construction trace as a selection history without loss (against Part IV, collapsing the two provenances and removing creativity from the semantics); or an argument that rules out that explanation operates on the object layer of Part IV.

The words: "A contains an edit that alters the relation reporting it without altering what it reports". The formula: exists a ∈ Alt_j∖Slc_j (an edit that alters j's relation... wait, Alt_j is edits altering L_j — j = asg(o) is the reporting component (o's assigner); "alters the relation reporting it" = alters L_j; "without altering what it reports" = m's assigner's relation unchanged, where m ∈ V_j∖{o}, i.e., m is a port read by j that o reports about.

Hmm, the words also say "that is, when the component assigning it has a measurement's signature (below)" — the words equate the A-condition with a signature condition; the formula drops that equation (D2.4's Vague notes the equation fails since (K) builds on C not A). The words state an equivalence (A-condition ⟺ signature); the new text states only the existential formula which is a version of the A-condition (with Alt_j, Slc_j inventions). Note also the formula quantifies over m ∈ V_j∖{o} with asg(m) defined — the words say "without altering what it reports" — but "what it reports" is presupposed, not existentially quantified in the words. The formula requires only existence of some m with unchanged relation; the words arguably required that the edit alters the reporting relation without altering what it reports (the specific thing reported). Let me be careful and check whether the formula matches D2.4 exactly: D2.4 has "L_asg(m)(a,b) = L_asg(m)(1,b) ∀b"; T1 writes "L_asg(m)(a,·)=L_asg(m)(1,·)" — same. The words: "an edit under which the two relations stay equal does not separate the components" — i.e., if under edit x the two (transported) relations are equal, then adding x to C doesn't separate them (they remain one kind on C∪{x}). The formula: j∼_C j′ by β with β_*L_j(x)=L_{j′}(x) gives j∼_{C∪{x}} j′. Note: β_*L_j(x) — should be β_*(L_j(x)) = the pushed-forward relation at edit x. content.thinking:
Now I have what I need for section (o). For O1–O5, I must propose fixes in one of the three forms (no new prose):

**O1 (L61)**: "(Suff) sufficiency of the four conditions of Account" — Q2 says four conditions not enough where link declared. Fix: text change replacing the span by its formal statement: "(Suff) sufficiency of \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\)" — replace "the four conditions of Account" with "Account(ℰ)∧¬Dec(t)". Exact old span: "(Suff) sufficiency of the four conditions of Account" → new "(Suff) sufficiency of \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\)" (D16.XV). Kind: formal.

**O2 (L49)**: "A piece of mathematics explains, relative to a question, when its components respond to those edits as the target structure does (Part VII)." Fix options: replace by formal statement adding ¬Dec(t)? The sentence defines "explains" for mathematics. Per Q2, meeting the response condition isn't enough if declared. The maths: Expl := Acc ∧ ¬Dec (FC30.new1(c) — "Expl := Acc ∧ ¬Dec meets both (Suff) and the owner's condition"). So the fix: replace the span "when its components respond to those edits as the target structure does" with "when it meets \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) and its components respond to those edits as the target structure does"? That adds prose. Better: replace with a pointer: "when it meets \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) (Part V, Part XV)". Hmm the three kinds: delete a span; replace by formal statement; replace by pointer. Proposal: replace "when its components respond to those edits as the target structure does (Part VII)" with "when it meets \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) on its question and contract (Part V; Part XV, (Suff))". Is that "formal statement" kind — yes, it's a formula replacing words. It drops the "components respond to those edits as the target structure does" gloss — that gloss is (F1) informally; (E) includes it. OK.

**O3 (L69)**: ""Explanation" in this commitment means an account, an explanatory candidate meeting \(\operatorname{Account}\) on its contract" — fix: replace "meeting \(\operatorname{Account}\) on its contract" with "meeting \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) on its contract".

**O4 (L397)**: "What a stated premise cannot do is stand in for the steps." — conflicts with Q23 (a single claim alone is an argument, no steps). Per Q23, the sentence is false as written? "A stated premise cannot stand in for the steps" — under Q23, there need be no steps; a premise alone is an argument. The sentence's intent (circularity block) is carried by D9.7's RO (the leaf conditions). Fix: delete the span. Check nothing depends on it: D9.7's block ("no leaf of α has ¬φ as a conjunct") carries the content. Deleting "What a stated premise cannot do is stand in for the steps. " — safe? The following sentence: "An argument does not rule out a claim when the claim's denial is among its premises..." stands alone. Yes, delete.

**O5 (L397)**: "A premise taken as given differs from such a premise in that the argument has steps from it to what it rules out: it finds that the candidate gives what the premise excludes." — the "in that the argument has steps from it to what it rules out" clashes with Q23 (no step needed). Fix: replace that span by its formal statement? The remaining content: "A premise taken as given ... : it finds that the candidate gives what the premise excludes." Hmm. The distinguishing feature per Q23/D9.7: a premise taken as given, unlike a premise that is the denial, does not have ¬φ as a conjunct — the block of D9.7. Replace "in that the argument has steps from it to what it rules out" with the formal statement of D9.7's block condition: "in that \(\neg\varphi\) is not a conjunct of it (D9.7)". So: old span "in that the argument has steps from it to what it rules out" → new "in that \(\neg\varphi\) is not a conjunct of it (D9.7)". Wait, but the sentence structure: "A premise taken as given differs from such a premise in that X: it finds that the candidate gives what the premise excludes." With X = "¬φ is not a conjunct of it (D9.7)". That works and stays within the kinds (formal).

**O6 (decision S27)**: The bare claim "is not enough for a creative agent to do anything about it" vs Q23+S28. The orchestrator's reading: triggering a conflict ≠ doing something about it (repairing). But under S28, "ruling out a rival by a claim taken as given is a choice that was made" and the owner said "Also, yes. That 'ruling out' is a choice that was made" in answer to "is ruling out a rival by a claim taken as given already doing something about it?" — wait, re-read S28: Claude asked whether ruling out a rival by a claim taken as given is already doing something about it; the owner answered "Also, yes. That 'ruling out' is a choice that was made." So the owner affirmed: ruling out IS doing something about it. And S27 says the bare claim alone "is not enough for a creative agent to do anything about it". The reconciliation (orchestrator's): the claim alone triggers a conflict but doesn't tell how to repair; using it to rule out is a choice, an act, but not the act of repairing.
